title: Tupp and the Jiggling Charm
markdown:
It was a morning of soft pale light on the pine-dark slopes of Owlglass Mountain. Tupp the young ogre felt a bit wobbly, like a cloud with a wobble. Moss-green skin not as cheerful as usual, patched-up tunic droopy. He had borrowed a very special Giggle-Charm from Imogen the Badger: a small smooth stone that always hummed with tiny laughter, a pocketful of sunshine. In his hurry to admire its jiggle, he had quite forgotten which of the many cozy caves, hidden like sleeping dormice homes, he had tucked it into. Worry fluttered like a trapped moth. Disappointing Imogen made his tummy flip-flop.

“I must find it.” A low rumble like distant thunder. Sturdy boots crunching fallen pine needles. Mountain air crisp: wet dirt, pine, a hint of wild thyme. Each step higher, clouds gathering like fluffy sheep.

Along a mossy path worn smooth by deer and foxes, a frantic voice: “Where, oh where, have they flown?” Tupp, about to look at a ladybug, peeked around a big grey rock like a giant’s forgotten teacup. A wizard with a beard as long and messy as a vine in moonlight, robes patched with twinkling starlight, patting pockets, looking under plants. Beside him a goat chewing thoughtfully. Silas’s goat, Gwendolyn.

“Good day, Wizard Silas. Are you looking for something important?”

Silas sighed like dry leaves. “My spectacles. Precious, sight-granting spectacles. I can’t see a thing. My potions are turning out strange.” He held up a bottle a worrying shade of purple, bubbling. “Meant to be yellow, like a buttercup bursting. Looks more like a grumpy cloud.”

Gwendolyn nudged his leg. Amber eyes: think harder. Silas gave her a fond if squinty smile.

Tupp scratched his moss-green head. Strange potions. Lost spectacles. Forgotten Giggle-Charm. A thought like a firefly. “When I’m happy, or when something makes me laugh, things sometimes seem to jiggle. Imogen the Badger’s Giggle-Charm hums with laughter, and it makes things around it feel bouncy.”

Silas blinked. “Jiggle, you say? My spectacles are small and roll easily. They like to skitter away like frightened mice. Maybe if they could jiggle out of their hiding place?” Gwendolyn nodded.

“I think I might have left it near my favourite thinking-rock. A big round one with soft moss. If I could just find that rock, and if I had the charm…” His voice trailed off.

“But you don’t have the charm. And I don’t have my glasses.” The purple potion fizzed.

A bright idea, quick as wild strawberries on a sunny patch. “What if my Giggle-Charm could help you find your spectacles? And maybe, if it jiggles things, it could help me remember where I put it myself.” A tricky thought, like yarn a kitten had played with.

Silas beamed. “A splendid idea. If only we had the charm.”

“Patience now.” Grandmother’s words. He closed his eyes, pictured the path, the trees, the rocks. He remembered sitting by a big mossy rock, humming a happy tune while he admired the charm. He walked a little further, Gwendolyn trotting, Silas peering hopefully at every shadow. There: a perfect round thinking-rock, thick emerald moss. Nestled beside it, winking in the sunlight, Imogen’s Giggle-Charm, humming louder, happy to be found.

Tupp picked it up. Warm, smooth, a thousand tiny giggles. He held it out. “Here, Wizard. Try this.”

Silas held it near the mossy ground where he thought he had lost his spectacles. The charm pulsed with soft happy laughter. Then, a tiny wiggle-thump, something glinted under a clover. The spectacles. They had rolled and hidden themselves.

Silas put them on. The world snapped into sharp focus. He blinked at the charm, at Tupp, at the charm again. He remembered Tupp’s words. Then, like a light in a dark sky, he remembered seeing Tupp place the charm carefully by the rock, right before the worry started. A jiggling memory, brought back by the charm.

“You put it right here, after you finished admiring it. Your memory must have been waiting for the charm to jiggle it awake.”

Tupp’s moss-green face broke into a wide grin. He had not forgotten after all. A little mountain magic, and a helping hoof. He took the humming charm back, lighter, like a dandelion seed. Silas adjusted his starlight-patched hat. Gwendolyn bleated, contented. The mountain air sighed.

And so Tupp returned Imogen the Badger’s Giggle-Charm, still humming. Kindness had jiggled two lost things into the same patch of moss.
characters: Tupp (young ogre who borrowed a giggle-charm), Silas (a wizard who loses his spectacles)
author: StoryGen Community
